translation: `Target` defines the proposition (`Prop`) asserting that `fls` is not derivable from the empty set of premises `∅` under the inductive derivability relation `Def15` (i.e., `¬ Def15 ∅ fls`; note that `Target` defines this proposition rather than asserting a proof of it). Over the language `Form` built from binary atomic formulas `atom r x y` (with `r, x, y : ℕ`), `fls`, `imp`, `all x` (`x : ℕ`), and `K`, `Def15 ∅` generates the set of formulas obtainable from the axiom set `Def14` using modus ponens (from `imp φ ψ` and `φ`, infer `ψ`), since the premise rule `φ ∈ ∅` can never apply and `Def15` has no other inference rules (in particular, no general universal generalization or `K`-necessitation rule). A formula belongs to `Def14` if and only if either (1) it is a closed formula (no natural-number variable `x` occurs free in it according to `Def6`/`Def13`) obtained by applying zero or more universal quantifiers `all x` (`Def12`) to a base axiom in `Def11`, or (2) it equals `K ψ` for some closed formula `ψ` obtained by applying zero or more universal quantifiers to a base axiom in `Def11`. The base axioms `Def11` are: (a) all formulas `φ` that hold under every valuation `v : Form → Prop` satisfying `¬ v fls` and `∀ φ ψ, v (imp φ ψ) ↔ (v φ → v ψ)` (`Def9`/`Def10`, i.e., propositional tautologies in `fls` and `imp`); (b) universal instantiation `imp (all x φ) (Def7 x y φ)` for all `x, y : ℕ` and `φ : Form` such that `y` is free for `x` in `φ` (`Def8 y x φ`, meaning no free occurrence of `x` in `φ` lies within the scope of `all y`, where `Def7 x y φ` replaces free occurrences of `x` with `y`); (c) quantifier distribution `imp (all x (imp φ ψ)) (imp (all x φ) (all x ψ))`; (d) vacuous generalization `imp φ (all x φ)` whenever `x` does not occur free in `φ`; (e) `imp (K (imp φ ψ)) (imp (K φ) (K ψ))`; (f) `imp (K φ) φ`; (g) `imp (K φ) (K (K φ))`; and (h) `imp (K (all x φ)) (all x (K φ))`. Thus `Target` is the proposition that `fls` is not in the closure of `Def14` under modus ponens.
